nextWork: Derive supported transaction-view/command response byte budgets, consume decoded streams within those budgets, and preserve parent cancellation, one request deadline, safe errors and same-command uncertain-outcome recovery.
limitations: The actual shared deadline helper runs in a deterministic Node VM using actual Node Response and ReadableStream with synthetic JSON and fetch.

The reader has a time deadline but no explicit body-byte ceiling. This witness records complete response.json consumption and a returned parsed object, not a violation of an existing declared size contract.
Synthetic status/MIME validation models the helper callback interface; this is not a transaction DTO, handler authorization or application-rendering test.
The returned padding is not claimed to be displayed or accepted by a caller. Each flow still applies its own validation and ownership rules.
Fixed wall/monotonic clocks isolate byte consumption. This does not measure latency, heap allocation or browser memory exhaustion.
No browser, listening server, database, provider, credentials, command execution, live network or deployment is used.
